chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughira, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not leave the four rak'at after the Maghrib prayer, neither in residency nor on a journey.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing voluntary prayers after Maghrib during travel?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the consistency of this specific supererogatory prayer by instructing believers to perform four voluntary rak'at after Maghrib regardless of whether they are in their home (hadr) or traveling (safar). This ruling highlights the enduring nature of this nafl prayer, distinguishing it from other voluntary acts that may be shortened or omitted during travel, thereby underscoring its significance in daily spiritual discipline.
